title: Assembly Hours
story: A machine is put together in numbered steps. steps lists, for each step, the steps that may only start after it is finished. Every step takes exactly one hour, and any number of steps that are ready can be done at the same time. How many hours does the whole job take at the least? If some steps end up waiting for each other in a circle, the job can never finish: report -1.

notes: A rule u -> v means v may only start after u is finished.

hints: A step can start once every step it waits for is done. Count, for each step, how many steps it still waits for; the steps with a count of 0 run in the first hour.
Keep a second list: the hour in which each step is done. When a step is done in hour h, every step that waits for it is done no earlier than hour h PLUS 1: keep the MAX.

Use a NEW QUEUE of ready steps. DEQUEUE a step, lower the count of each of its NEIGHBORS, and ENQUEUE a neighbor when its count reaches 0. The answer is the largest hour, or -1 if fewer steps left the queue than NODE COUNT.
edgeCases: a step that waits for a short chain and a long chain
a circle that the first steps lead into
a circle with no step free to start
